conviction_note: Small negative lean (p_up 44 on an 8% absolute move, so -0.96 scaled) resting mainly on a BLS proxy: hot-rolled long-product steel inputs rose about 5.4% quarter on quarter in Jul-Sep 2026 while steel wire output prices rose about 1%, which extends the cost-over-price squeeze management described in Q3. Two things partly offset it. Q4 is a 14-week quarter (fiscal 2026 ends Saturday 3 Oct 2026 under the 10-K's 'Saturday closest to September 30' rule), and a GAAP closure charge of roughly $0.05 is likely, which the market will look through. Findings sum to -0.5. The scaled number is close to it in size and sign, and both are small because the main evidence is a proxy and the name's EPS bar has only two estimates.
bar: Q4 FY26 (Sep-2026 quarter) EPS consensus $0.49 (2 analysts, range $0.47-$0.51, unchanged over 90 days) and revenue $201.31M (2 analysts, $196.1M-$206.5M), year-ago EPS $0.75 and revenue $177.44M: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/IIIN/analysis/ (read 2026-10-21). Revenue on its own is more likely a small beat (+2%).

findings.finding: BLS PPI shows the input-output spread narrowing again in IIIN's fiscal Q4 (Jul-Sep 2026 against Apr-Jun). Hot-rolled steel bars, plates and structural shapes (WPU101704, the closest public series to wire rod) averaged 313.9 against 297.7 (+5.4%). Steel wire (WPU101705) averaged 388.0 against 384.3 (+1.0%), and steel wire drawing industry output (PCU331222331222) 323.6 against 321.7 (+0.6%). Consensus EPS of $0.49 sits above Q3's $0.46, which implies flat-to-better margins after Q3 gross margin fell to 10.2% from 17.1% on 'inflation across nearly all cost areas' that outran pricing. September output prices did tick up (wire 391.1, drawing 325.3), consistent with price increases landing late in the quarter, which mainly helps Q1 FY27 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin and EPS misses have been sold hard: -22.1% on 2026-04-16 (EPS $0.27 against $0.64) and -19.23% on 2025-10-16 (EPS $0.75 against $0.79). The near-in-line Q3 (+3.4% EPS surprise) moved +1.28% on 2026-07-16. The only large up move was +13.81% on 2025-04-17.
findings.source: https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/WPU101705 (steel wire). Same API for WPU101704, title at https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/WPU101704, and for PCU331222331222.
findings.why_not_priced: A two-analyst EPS bar that has not moved in 90 days and sits above Q3 has not marked inputs to the Jul-Sep steel series. If the market had priced continued compression, the consensus would sit below $0.46 and the stock would have fallen into the print rather than rising 3.5% over 20 days. Part of it may be in the -20% from the 52-week high.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The company has not confirmed Q4 rod costs. The direction matches management's own Q3 statement that wire rod, freight and other costs rose faster than prices (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/764401/000143774926023670/ex_988377.htm), but the PPI understated IIIN's own Q3 pricing gap (IIIN ASP +2.3% q/q against drawing PPI +4.8%), so the mapping is loose. Weighted-average inventory costing on a $167M inventory (built $29M in nine months) lags and smooths rod cost changes. That cuts both ways: an earlier pre-buy at lower cost would cushion Q4.

findings.finding: Fiscal Q4 2026 is a 14-week quarter. The 10-K says 'Our fiscal year is the 52 or 53 weeks ending on the Saturday closest to September 30', and the Saturday closest to Wednesday 30 Sep 2026 is 3 Oct 2026. FY2023-FY2025 were all 52-week years. The extra week alone adds about 7.7% to shipments. The revenue consensus of $201.3M is only 1.8% above Q3's 13-week $197.7M and about 13.5% over the year-ago $177.4M, against ASP running about +8% y/y. That leaves room for a revenue beat of roughly 2-6% if per-week volume held, though the extra week also carries a week of fixed cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior 53-week quarter in the 7-print baseline. Revenue-led beats without margin have been bought little: Q3 FY26 grew revenue +9.9% y/y with a near-in-line EPS and moved +1.28%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is unclear whether either of the two analysts included the 14th week. A revenue consensus barely above a seasonally strong 13-week Q3 suggests at most part of it. If it were fully in, consensus revenue would be around $210M+, not $201M. The year-ago comparison is 13 weeks, so y/y growth will flatter the headline.
findings.independence: The Q3 release data (shipments +11.9% sequential, ASP +8.0% y/y) supports the per-week run-rate arithmetic: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/764401/000143774926023670/ex_988377.htm. There is no independent confirmation of Q4 volume, and the release noted data-center project delays.

findings.finding: The Upper Sandusky, Ohio welded-wire closure (8-K item 2.05, 2026-08-21) carries about $4.6M of restructuring: $1.0M non-cash impairment, $0.4M severance, $2.5M equipment relocation and $0.7M other. The decision fell inside fiscal Q4, so the impairment and severance (about $1.4M pre-tax, roughly $0.055 a share on about 19.4M shares) are likely recognized in Q4. Relocation and other cash costs are expected from Q1 FY27. That makes GAAP Q4 EPS mechanically lower than a pre-charge $0.49 estimate, and it is unclear whether the two analysts include it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: IIIN discloses the EPS impact of restructuring every time (Q3 FY25: $0.9M, $0.03 a share). No print in the baseline turned on a restructuring line.
findings.why_not_priced: Headline GAAP EPS against a stale two-analyst bar could read as a miss in screens. Because the company quantifies the charge, most of this should be looked through, which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: Same 8-K as the following finding (the savings side of the same closure). They are counted once each in opposite directions because they land on different lines: this one on the reported quarter's one-off charge, the next on the forward cost base.

findings.finding: The same closure moves Upper Sandusky volume into plants with 'ample open capacity', with up to 65 positions cut and operations ending by end-October 2026. The CEO said 'We do not expect this action to affect the Company's revenue.' Savings were not quantified in August. If management quantifies them on the 10:00 ET call, that gives FY27 margin support at the moment the market is focused on margin recovery.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: IIIN gives no numeric guidance, and its outlook commentary has moved the stock mainly through margins (the -22.1% and -19.23% prints). Earlier consolidation (EWP acquisition, Warren facility closure) carried no separately attributable reaction in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The closure itself is public (announced 8 weeks ago). Only a first quantification of savings would be new. If the market already credited savings, the stock would not have drifted from about $32.6 (14 Aug Form 4 price) to $30.3 after the announcement.
findings.independence: Shares the 21 Aug 2026 8-K with the charge finding above. There is no other source.

findings.finding: SVP and COO Richard Wagner sold 1,640 shares at $30.3071 on 2026-08-27 (Form 144 filed 08-24), leaving 40,000 shares, about 4% of his position, inside the fiscal Q4 quarter and after the closure decision. The other August Form 4s (CEO Woltz and four others, 08-12 and 08-18) are RSU vestings with tax withholding (CEO: 5,647 vested, 1,473 withheld at $32.62), not discretionary trades.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and tiny. It is filed only because a discretionary sale by the operating chief inside the quarter is a weak signal in one direction, and a judge may weigh it differently.
findings.independence: CEO Form 4 showing a non-discretionary vesting: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/764401/000101747526000010/0001017475-26-000010.txt. It points nowhere directionally.

outside_window.finding: Cash costs of the Upper Sandusky closure ($2.5M equipment relocation plus $0.7M other) are expected to run from Q1 FY27 through the rest of fiscal 2027. That weighs on FY27 GAAP results, which the market will see in January 2027.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The small negative lean cuts against the modest 20-day run-up (+3.45%) and an unmoved consensus above Q3, but it sits with the stock's 20% discount to its 52-week high, which may already price some of the margin squeeze.
lessons_applied: Rule 2 (one-offs): the restructuring charge finding went from -0.3 to -0.2, because IIIN quantifies such charges and there is no path from it to the guide.
Rule 8 and the core's understatement note: abs_move_pct went from 7.5 to 8.0 on a two-analyst name whose misses have moved -19% to -22%.
Rule 5 (proxy): the BLS spread finding stays at -1.2, filed as a proxy with its independence stating so. It was not shrunk again, because it was already sized as a proxy in the draft.
Rules 6 and 7 changed nothing: the bar has two agreeing estimate sources ($0.49), and short interest (4.57%, 4.77 days) is not crowded.
